I have some old junk computers lying around. Not the stuff that came from new egg but real honest to goodness IBM Servers. So I got to looking at my stash and found an old X 346 just setting under a thick coating of dust. The reason I never did any thing with it was that it was minus the drives. You know those Ultra 320 80 pin SCSI 10K rpm drives were dammed expensive. Well not any more. I just picked up 6 300 GB U320 80 pin SCSI drives for about $150. So now I got the thing to power up.

The next thing to do is make the RAID because the thing uses the IBM ServRAID card 6M with a bunch of cashe. Well I got a the severRAID software CD, (You boot it up and make the RAID before you load any operating System), and created a RAID 5 configuration. The nice thing about this box is that it has a internal DDS5 (DAT72) 1/4 inch tape drive. The data tapes for his drive aren't to bad. By the way I have successfully loaded AIX version 3 off a tape that was 20 years old, so tape is definitely Ultra long storage.

Now What operating system to use. Well the 346 had the windows Server 2003 sticker on it but I don't want to go that route. So I thought about going with a Linux Distro. (The 346 has two 3.6 Ghertz dual core XEON processosrs in it, and 4 two gig sticks of ram) But I decided that I really want to play around with the ZFS file system by SUN. So I have decided to run the X86 version of Solaris 11.2.

I downloaded the OS from SUN and have it now an a CD. I plan on installing it in the next few days. I will let every one know just what happened in this project. I think that I will use this thing has a back up server for storing backups from my other systems.

Oh by the way I bought one of the Cheapie 4 port KVM boxes and set it up. I now have two windows boxes, a laptop (in a docking station) and my X346 on it. It took a day to get every thing worked out but it works now. The biggest problem was electrical interference on the VGA cables that showed up on the screen. I am using ferrite core filtered VGA cables and that seems to have fixed or at least reduced the problem to where it is not as noticeable now.

You can get much more recent and more powerful servers like that off eBay for incredibly cheap.

Currently, I have a dell poweredge r905 running in my closet. It's super loud and huge, but its really powerful and great to use. Specs are 4x quadcore 2.4ghz xeon E7330 processors, 128gb of ddr2 ECC memory, 2x 1570w power supplies and 5x 300gb 15k rpm SAS drives hooked up to a raid controller witha battery backup (massively important for raid). Right now its running plex on Ubuntu 15.04 with lubuntu netbook desktop. Future upgrades include modding it to fit in a 750ti, getting the audio card working (the drivers are from when the server was new), and eventually upgrading the processors to hexacores.

Also, OP, you can't really take advantage of ZFS and all its stuff with any kind of hardware or software raid involved, ZFS and BTRFS (which is pretty similar) need direct access to the drives. You could probably find an old SAN without too much trouble, because everyone is getting rid of fibre channel and replacing it with 10gbit, and that would give you a much better way to play around with ZFS.
